name: Scientific Writer and Grant Development Specialist

companyDescription.title: Company Description
companyDescription.text:
By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

Why join Harvard Medical School?

Harvard Medical School's mission is to nurture a diverse, inclusive community dedicated to alleviating suffering and improving health and well-being for all through excellence in teaching and learning, discovery and scholarship, and service and leadership.

You’ll be at the heart of biomedical discovery, education, and innovation, working alongside world-renowned faculty and a community dedicated to improving human health. This is more than a job - it’s an opportunity to shape the future of medicine.

jobDescription.title: Job Description
jobDescription.text:
The Department of Neurobiology seeks a Scientific Writer & Grant Development Specialist. Reporting to the Executive Director of Research, the scientific writer will help translate complex neurobiology research into clear, accurate, and compelling written materials for scientific, institutional, and general audiences. This position is ideal for a PhD-level neuroscientist who is interested in a career in scientific writing, research development, grant support, or academic communications. The successful candidate will contribute to multiple projects, gain exposure to the grant-development process, and work collaboratively with faculty and administrative colleagues. We seek a candidate who has expertise in neurobiology and familiarity with sensory systems in animal models and methods in neurobiological research.  

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Grant Application Support 

  • Assist faculty with the preparation and revision of grant proposals, progress reports, letters of recommendation, research summaries, and related materials for cross-institutional grants.
  •  Review proposal drafts for clarity, organization, grammar, consistency, and alignment with sponsor guidelines. 
  • Help compile background information, references, preliminary data summaries, and supporting materials.
  • Track proposal deadlines and assist with maintaining proposal development schedules. 
  • Support the preparation of resubmissions and responses to reviewer comments.
  • Coordinate with faculty and research administration staff to gather information and ensure materials are complete.

Funding Opportunity Research

  • Search for and summarize relevant funding opportunities from federal agencies, foundations, nonprofit organizations, and other sponsors.
  • Prepare brief funding opportunity summaries for faculty and department leadership. 
  • Assist with assessing eligibility requirements, deadlines, funding priorities, and submission guidelines.
  • Help identify potential funding mechanisms that align with faculty research interests.
  • Support the preparation of materials for internal funding competitions and limited-submission opportunities.

Scientific Writing

  • Assist with preparing summaries of laboratory for research centers, initiatives, and collaborative projects. 
  • Review written materials for scientific accuracy, readability, and consistency of tone.
  • Conduct literature searches and prepare background summaries as needed. 
  • Help organize and maintain shared writing resources, templates, and reference materials.

Administrative and Project Support

  • Participate in meetings with faculty and staff to gather information and clarify project goals.
  • Maintain organized files and documentation for writing and proposal-development projects.
  • Track assignments, deadlines, and revisions across multiple projects.
  • Communicate project updates and identify potential delays or information gaps.
  • Write and edit progress reports for active funding opportunities. 
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

qualifications.title: Qualifications
qualifications.text:
Basic Qualifications

  • Minimum five years of related professional experience. Higher education may count towards experience.

Additional Qualifications and Skills:

Preferred Qualifications

  • PhD in neuroscience, neurobiology, biomedical sciences, or a related field is highly desirable.
  • Strong foundation in neuroscience research and terminology.
  • Demonstrated ability to write clearly and accurately about scientific topics.
  • Experience writing or editing scientific documents, such as manuscripts, dissertations, grant materials, reports, or presentations.
  • Strong proofreading and editing skills.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines.
  • Ability to work collaboratively and accept feedback.
  • Proficiency with standard word processing, presentation, spreadsheet, and online research tools.
  • Strong grasp of neurobiology methodologies, specifically in the context of physiology, molecular biology and genetics, sensory systems, and animal behavior.
  • Experience working in a university, research institute, or other scientific environment.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Ability to understand and synthesize complex scientific information.
  • Ability to adapt writing style for faculty, scientific reviewers, donors, administrators, and general audiences.
  • Willingness to learn institutional proposal processes and sponsor requirements.
  • Ability to ask effective questions and gather information from subject-matter experts.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality concerning unpublished research, grant concepts, and donor information.
  • Comfort working in a deadline-oriented environment with frequent shifting priorities.

Position Scope

  • This is an entry-level scientific writing and research development position.
  • The successful candidate will receive guidance and mentorship while gradually developing responsibility for individual writing assignments and project areas.
  • The role is primarily focused on supporting faculty and departmental activities rather than independently leading grant strategy or managing major proposal portfolios.

additionalInformation.text:

Work Format Details

This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that all duties and responsibilities must be performed at a Harvard or Harvard-designated location. Certain visa types may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment.

Salary Grade and Ranges

This position is salary grade level 056. Please visit  Harvard's Salary Ranges  to view the corresponding salary range and related information. 

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision health insurance coverage starting on day one 
  • Retirement plans with university contributions 
  • Wellbeing and mental health resources 
  • Support for families and caregivers 
  • Professional development opportunities including tuition assistance and reimbursement 
  • Commuter benefits, discounts and campus perks 

Learn more about these and additional benefits on our Benefits & Wellbeing Page.
